title: Lewis and Clark's salt works
h1: Lewis and Clark's salt works, winter 1805-1806: what the journals record
dek: Five kettles, three salt makers and the Clatsop and Nehalem Tillamook families who lived beside them. What the journals and the park record say, where they disagree, and why this is not a way to make salt.
description: How the Corps of Discovery made salt on the Oregon coast in 1805-1806, per the journals and park sources, with the Clatsop and Tillamook neighbours named accurately.
recheck: If any listed source changes, when the intervening journal entries (including Clark's January visit to the salt camp) are read directly, or when a Clatsop or Tillamook-authored account of the winter is found.

safety_review.scope: Taxonomy does not gate this item, but the page carries a safety-verdict panel (not-validated: seawater salt-making and home salting) and no process, quantity or time instructions. Requested for human read-through of the verdict panel and the editor's note on boiling and dissolved contaminants.
